newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain's emir opens new Shura council session.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain's emir opens new Shura council session.

text.p: Bahrain's Emir Sheikh Isa bin Sulman al-Khalifa on Tuesday opened the first session of a newly appointed Shura council, saying he hoped it would work together with the government to promote development in Bahrain.

Sheikh Isa on Saturday appointed 40 members to the consultative council to replace a 30-member body appointed in 1992. The new council widens popular representation and is to have a greater say in the Gulf island's affairs.
"We hope that the new council, with its expanded authority and popular representation, will be able to cooperate with the government...," Sheikh Isa told the council's opening session.

He said he hoped it would assist the government "in providing proposals and reviewing draft laws and projects to push ahead the country's development in various fields and to carry out development plans and projects".
The council gives its view on laws drafted by Bahrain's cabinet before they are sent to the emir for final approval. An elected assembly was dissolved by the government in 1975.
Sheikh Isa said Bahrain had succeeded to contain unrest by "a foreign-backed group which tried to undermine its achievement and unity".
He was apparently referring to anti-government protests by members of the Shi'ite Moslem community which broke out in 1994. Restoration of the dissolved parliament is one of the dissidents demands.
Bahrain, the Gulf's main financial and banking centre, has accused Shi'ite Iran of trying to topple its government.
Sheikh Isa thanked "all brothers and friends who backed our measures to maintain security and stability in this country which we will, God willing, defend by all means".
